args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. Note: the v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. We rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying it, and check why the release went to production even though the release candidate was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again.

- **Cause:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. A recheck shows v2.3.0 running in all three regions, passing health checks, with a 0.2% error rate.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It also says two things need to happen before v2.3.1 is deployed again: find why it failed, and find out how it reached production even though its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also failing in staging.

No approval was needed, since v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
